profile_md: Provision found so far at Essex is led by **iTeams**, an extracurricular programme run by Essex Startups in which multidisciplinary student teams tackle challenges set by external businesses, mentored by industry experts, and present a report and pitch to a panel. It is selective (limited places, application), not credit-bearing as evidenced, and the latest evidenced edition is February 2025 (7 weeks, three businesses, six teams); a bespoke Cyber Innovate to Elevate variant connecting MSc/PhD students with SMEs ran to February 2026 but its team structure and outputs are not confirmed. Within Essex Business School, the Marketing Management module has students undertake a consultancy project for a real-world business, but whether this is group-based and how clients participate is not established; the MBA consultancy project is individual. Computer Science has a team project module without external clients and an individual capstone that can use company briefs. The Industry and Placements team promotes employer-led project briefs and live-project work-based learning (cited on Science and Health degree pages) but specific modules were not identified. The Big Essex Award is an employability award, excluded. Engineering, science, social science and law/health provision were not searched because the search limit was reached, so this review is Partial. Whether Essex has several distributed routes or a mainly extracurricular central one remains uncertain.
